title: Comparatives and Superlatives Quiz 2
description: Use the, -est and most, and choose in or of.
instructions: Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: 'Mount Everest is ___ mountain in the world.'
options: most high
the higher
the highest
highest
questions.explanation: A superlative needs the, and high is short so it adds -est. Watch out: the highest, not highest alone.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: She is the intelligentest student in the class.
She is the most intelligent student in the class.
She is the more intelligent student in the class.
She is most intelligent student in the class.
questions.explanation: Intelligent has more than two syllables, so the most is used. Watch out: -est is not added to long adjectives.

questions.question: This is {{1}} (cheap) shop in town.
questions.explanation: Cheap is short, so the cheapest. Watch out: the is needed before the superlative.

questions.question: It was {{1}} (exciting) film of the year.
questions.explanation: Exciting has three syllables, so the most exciting.

questions.question: We use 'in' with a place or group (in the class) and 'of' with a number of things (of the three).
questions.explanation: He is the tallest in the class; he is the tallest of the three. Watch out: of the class is not used.

questions.question: Complete the table.
questions.explanation: Each adjective follows its own pattern. Watch out: busy changes y to i.

questions.question: When do we use 'the most'?
options: with all adjectives of one syllable
with adjectives that are irregular
with adjectives of three syllables or more
with adjectives that end with -y
questions.explanation: Long adjectives take most. Watch out: short adjectives take -est.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The superlative is introduced by the, and the group follows with in.

questions.question: Match each ending with its use.
questions.explanation: These are the building blocks of the superlative. Watch out: the is placed before the superlative.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: This is the more beautiful place I have ever seen.
accepted: This is the most beautiful place I have ever seen.
This is the most beautiful place I have ever seen
questions.explanation: A superlative uses most, not more. Watch out: more compares two things.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: It is the most long river in Africa.
It is the longest river in Africa.
It is the longer river in Africa.
It is longest river in Africa.
questions.explanation: Long is short, so the longest. Watch out: the is needed.

questions.question: Which are superlatives?
options: the smallest
more useful
the most useful
smaller
questions.explanation: A superlative has the and -est or most. Watch out: smaller and more useful are comparatives.
